text:
Assistant A provides a more accurate, structured, and comprehensive response. It correctly identifies the key US statutes (Sherman, Clayton, FTC Acts) and Chinese legislation (AML 2008, SAMR enforcement), and offers a nuanced comparison of enforcement mechanisms (including private litigation differences). Its case studies are factually sound: the Microsoft case accurately describes the bundling allegations and settlement, and the Qualcomm case effectively illustrates parallel enforcement in both jurisdictions with correct details (the $975 million Chinese fine and the 2020 US appellate reversal).

Assistant B, while covering similar ground, contains significant factual errors—most notably regarding the Didi Chuxing case, which it incorrectly attributes to the NDRC (dissolved in 2018) in 2018 with a 2020 settlement, when in fact SAMR fined Didi in 2022. It also lacks the depth of comparative analysis and misses the opportunity to use Qualcomm as a direct cross-jurisdictional case study. Assistant A’s discussion of China’s “socialist market economy” objective and private enforcement differences adds valuable context that B omits.

[[A]]
